results.finding: sections, unit counts and unit forms match the spec

Audited all 83 aligned units p01–p83 against the independent outline, in order, and retained the introduction callout as unmapped evidence. Every summary matches its controlling idea when its attached material is included: the short prompt labels at p31, p33, p46, p48, p51 and p53 introduce the quoted examples, and the concise p21 summary is developed by the human/AI comparison table. There are no missing, reordered, or extraneous prose/list units.

Audited p01–p83 and the opening callout; the outliner flagged no unit as having two ideas. The roadmap p07 has one signposting function, the lists at p08, p16, p56, p74–p76 and p79 each develop one organizing idea, and the multiple task examples in p27 and p78 demonstrate one scale or selection principle rather than unrelated topics.

Audited every unit and attached callout: p01–p07 establish and preview C1–C6; p08–p14 support C1; p15–p23 support C2; p24–p29 support C3; p30–p54 support C4; p55–p65 support C5; p66–p78 support C6; p79 applies C3/C5/C6; p80–p83 synthesize and hand off C3–C6. The internal writing and architecture references illustrate inspectable intent, and the final capabilities link concerns the people who retain the decisions, so neither detours from the thesis.

Audited all 34 declared evidence items and the actual draft attachments: nine quotations (p01, p04, p08, p31, p33, p46, p48, p51, p53), eight tables (p13, p21, p25, p34, p42, p49, p54, p57), five figures (p06, p12, p35, p39, p58), seven source uses (p01, p03, p15, p40, p41, p66, p83), three examples (p02, p27, p78), and two scenarios (p45, p50). Captions explain all five figures; each prompt pair is interpreted by the following analysis and comparison; table headings, explanatory columns, framing and subsequent synthesis connect the rows to the argument. For example, p34 explains the prompt elements as leadership functions, p43 says where spec fields concentrate judgment, and p55 explicitly identifies the retained human approval across both review examples. Source references state their contribution locally; this judgment concerns explanation in the draft, not external factual verification.

Audited all 82 declared boundaries: 68 paragraph transitions and 14 section/conclusion transitions. The text carries command limits into Marquet, legibility into the analogy boundary, the two extremes into level choice, clearer language into a written contract, and the review examples into the autonomy gates; the grouped failure modes and role applications keep their shared subjects visible, and the practice proceeds from framing to AI response before synthesis. At p45 the quoted written decision frame supplies the declared example relationship, although flow reader 1 wants its status as a spec made more explicit; that narrower reading friction is recorded separately. The final hand-off carries boundaries into the human capabilities needed to set them.

Compared both independent accounts with the post prerequisite order and all 13 section flow declarations. Both recover problem → model and limits → level choice → language/specification → parallel applications → controls/failures → roles/practice/self-assessment → synthesis, and both explain why each stage belongs there. The comparison, grouping and chronological patterns are also recovered; neither reader recommends reordering. All passages other than the two separately recorded, uncorroborated local pauses were followable to both readers.

Audited first uses throughout p01–p83 for the technology-leadership readership named in the prose; the supplied spec has no separate audience.already_knows or audience.does_not_know inventory. Intent and specs are unpacked in the introduction, the human model is explained before the seven levels, level numbers are defined before applications, observability and rollback are explained before higher-autonomy examples, event-driven architecture/decoupling/eventual consistency are glossed in the architecture example, agentic behavior is defined in its failure-mode paragraph, and agency/judgment/persuasion are glossed before the hand-off. Linked neighboring essays are summarized locally rather than required for comprehension; neither flow reader reports an unexplained term.

Audited the opening callout and p01–p07. The opening ties a concrete product-decision problem to retained human responsibility, states the command-to-intent claim, defines its main terms and gives a specific roadmap. It is not a placeholder, restated assignment question, dictionary opening, sweeping historical opening or book report.

Audited Final Thought p80–p83 and the following reference list. The ending combines ladder/spec/guardrails, explains their decision value, gives a one-interaction action and hands off to capabilities already introduced at p07 and p66. It neither unveils a late thesis or new evidence nor ends on a rephrased thesis alone; the optional references do not reopen the argument.

Final Thought p80–p83 combines three earlier functions: the ladder selects delegated work, a spec exposes intent, and guardrails preserve observability. The resulting gain is work people can understand, judge and own, developed in p81 as better shared decisions rather than artifact volume; p82 makes that implication actionable through one interaction.

Checked the declared callback against Introduction p02–p06 and Final Thought p80–p83. The opening asks what intent, boundaries and review consequential work requires; the ending answers with the combined ladder/spec/control approach and the explicit instruction to make one interaction’s boundaries and review visible before asking AI to act.

The introduction-only reader accurately predicts all 13 body sections in roadmap order, followed by the synthesis and hand-off. Their expected conceptual source, interaction contrasts, inspectable specifications, architecture/delivery scenarios and practical leadership tone match the body; the draft does not instead deliver experiments or measured performance claims. The reader’s question about the ladder’s provenance does not alter the accurately predicted subject, evidence type or progression.

The AC-1 reader selects Level 1 for narrow, low-risk formatting and explicitly rejects maximizing autonomy. For an important workflow they require an intent spec, representative competence evidence, bounded permissions, an audit trail, consequential review, escalation and recovery before Level 6; they reserve Level 7 for continuous operation in a mature controlled workflow and reduce autonomy when prerequisites are missing. This matches the expected task-sensitive choice.

The AC-2 reader rewrites the request around an owned approval decision, operating context, constraints, alternatives, evaluation criteria, allowed actions, review and escalation. They also ask AI to restate assumptions and clarify before assessment, and identify consequential work as requiring a short reviewable contract before execution; all elements of the expected inspectable agreement are recovered.

The AC-3 reader retains purpose, contextual judgment, legitimate trade-offs, approval, acceptable risk, trust and consequences with people. Their controls include explicit scope and permissions, representative competence checks, reconstructable logs, review stops, escalation, rollback or containment, and a named accountable owner, with lower autonomy when intent, competence or control is missing. This matches every required accountability and scaling-control element.
